items.title: US Department of Labor honors 772 employers committed to veterans’ employment with 2026 HIRE Vets Medallion Awards
items.summary: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor recognized 772 employers for their commitment to employing and supporting the nation’s service members by presenting them with the 2026 Honoring Investments in Recruiting and Employing American Military Veterans Medallion Award.U.S. Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling and Assistant Secretary for Veterans’ Employment and Training Service Jeremiah Workman presented the awards, which recognize employers for their commitment to supporting U.S. military veterans in the civilian workforce, during a Nov. 12 ceremony at the Frances Perkins Building in Washington. “Veterans are our nation’s heroes and bring proven leadership, a strong work ethic, and the ability to perform under pressure – all valuable skills for employers,” said Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. “Under President Trump, the U.S. Department of Labor’s Veterans’ Employment and Training Service is working to ensure employers can access this exceptional talent while helping veterans secure high-skill, high-paying jobs.”Signed into law by President Donald Trump in 2017, the HIRE Vets Medallion Program is the only federal-level program recognizing veteran employment and emplo

items.title: US Department of Labor issues guidance to employers, plan fiduciaries on inaccurate health network provider directories
items.summary: WASHINGTON – As part of its effort to protect workers, retirees, and their families, the U.S. Department of Labor today issued an enforcement alert to help employers and plan fiduciaries ensure plan participants and beneficiaries are receiving accurate provider directories for in-network coverage.Health plans and insurance issuers are required under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act to regularly verify, update, and publish accurate provider directory information. The enforcement alert provides best practices and questions to ask so that participants and beneficiaries are protected from unexpected out-of-network costs and receive quicker access to care from in-network providers.“President Trump is committed to improving the quality and lowering the cost of healthcare for all hardworking Americans. With this guidance, the U.S. Department of Labor is letting health plans and insurance issuers know that they must do better,” said Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. “They must provide accurate and updated information so that American workers, retirees, and their families can make informed healthcare decisions.
